note: Versions each base image's own pip resolves for the packages task Dockerfiles install, keyed "<base>|<index>". Resolved with pip --dry-run --ignore-installed --no-deps --report so nothing is installed, against the index the task names rather than PyPI globally: the pytorch CPU index serves different builds than PyPI, and the bases carry different interpreters (Python 3.11.2 on bench-base:node-22, 3.12.13 on bench-base:python-3.12, 3.12.3 on bench-base:ubuntu-24.04), so a global latest can be wrong for the image that has to install it.
apt_note: apt packages are deliberately not pinned. Debian and Ubuntu rotate their archives, so an exact version pin stops resolving once that version is published out, converting silent drift into a hard build failure across the 209 tasks that apt-get install. Reproducible apt needs a snapshot mirror or vendored .debs; until then the toolchain layer floats and is recorded here as a known gap rather than pinned into breakage.
base_image_note: The three bench-base images are built from bases/*.Dockerfile, which are committed, but their own FROM lines are floating tags (python:3.12-slim, ubuntu:24.04, node:22-slim) and the images exist only in the local docker store with no RepoDigests, so a fresh clone cannot rebuild them byte-identically. Recorded image IDs are the ones the v3.4/v3.5 records were produced against.

bench-base:python-3.12.drift: Shares ZERO layers with the pinned digest. Upstream python:3.12-slim moved between 2026-09-02 and the pin, and the original digest was never recorded because the image was tagged locally and carries no RepoDigests. Rebuilding from the pin yields a different base than the one the published records were produced against, so the oracle census and the negative control must be re-run before records built on it are published.

bench-base:ubuntu-24.04.drift: None. Shares every upstream layer with the pinned digest.

bench-base:node-22.drift: None. Shares every upstream layer with the pinned digest.

not_pinned.apt: 161 distinct packages across 209 task Dockerfiles and all three bases. Debian and Ubuntu rotate their archives, so an exact version pin stops resolving once that version is published out, which would convert silent drift into a hard build failure. Reproducible apt needs a snapshot mirror or vendored .debs.
